external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A grocery loyalty programme member who uses the mobile app and authorizes partner apps.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members collect points when they shop and spend them on gift cards.

external_entities.name: phone
external_entities.description: A member's phone on which the mobile app keeps a refresh token.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The app keeps a refresh token on the phone.

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: Mobile application used by members to sign in and call the rewards API.
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

processes.name: authorization server
processes.description: Authorization server that signs members in, issues authorization codes, refresh tokens and access tokens, and manages partner consents.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow

processes.name: rewards API
processes.description: API that reads and writes the points ledger and receives access-token-authenticated requests.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
processes.notes: It writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

processes.name: partner app
processes.description: A web application run by another company that obtains authorization and can show a member's points.
processes.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers
processes.notes: The partnerships team registers each partner app by hand and gives it a client ID and a client secret.

processes.name: browser
processes.description: A browser used by a member to sign in and approve consent for a partner app.
processes.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser

processes.name: support console
processes.description: A web application that closes a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.
processes.notes: It is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

data_stores.name: identity database
data_stores.description: Database containing member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database

data_stores.name: points ledger
data_stores.description: Ledger containing every member's balance and every points transaction, including the client that made each change.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: Store containing every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs a member in through the authorization server using the authorization code flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API with an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back
data_flows.data_description: Rewards API requests and access tokens

data_flows.name: approve consent
data_flows.description: A member signs in and approves the partner app consent screen at the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen

data_flows.name: request token
data_flows.description: The partner app sends token requests containing its client secret to the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.data_description: Token requests, client secret, authorization codes and tokens

data_flows.name: return code
data_flows.description: The browser returns an authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.

data_flows.name: show points
data_flows.description: The partner app accesses the rewards API to show a member's points.
data_flows.source_excerpt: such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points.

data_flows.name: manage identity
data_flows.description: The authorization server stores and updates accounts, credentials, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
data_flows.data_description: Accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents

data_flows.name: update ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes member balances and points transactions in the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

data_flows.name: write logs
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes each received request and its headers to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: obtain token
data_flows.description: The support console takes access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It takes access tokens from the same authorization server

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.

trust_boundaries.name: own cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The cloud account in which the platform components and stores run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account

trust_boundaries.name: members' phones
trust_boundaries.description: The members' phones, which are outside the system's own cloud account.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: apart from the members' phones and the partner apps.

trust_boundaries.name: partner apps' own servers
trust_boundaries.description: Servers run by other companies for their partner applications.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The identity database contains confidential data because it stores member personal data and credentials.
assumptions.basis: The text states that it contains member accounts, email addresses and password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger contains confidential data because it stores member-related financial and operating records.
assumptions.basis: The text states that it holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store contains confidential data because request headers may contain credentials and the logged requests may contain member data.
assumptions.basis: The text states that every request received by the rewards API, headers included, is written to the API log store.

assumptions.assumption: The rewards API is internet-facing because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The text states that the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The support console is internet-facing because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The text states that the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.
